title: Implement VPC endpoints module + DNS behavior defaults for Redwood Private (alpha)
creator: Irene Choi
content:
Context / Problem
- A recurring pilot failure mode is customers running fully-private subnets (no IGW / no NAT / strict egress) and then the installer fails during image pulls, token exchange (STS), or log shipping due to missing VPC endpoints or incorrect private DNS settings.
- We need an opinionated VPC endpoints module with Redwood-validated defaults and *controlled* DNS behavior. This needs to align with both:
  - Security guidance (least-privilege + no accidental public egress)
  - Installer expectations / preflight checks (clear required endpoints + warnings)

Scope
- Add `modules/vpc_endpoints` that can be composed with `modules/vpc` (subnets, route tables, NAT strategy).
- Provide defaults appropriate for Redwood Private on AWS with EKS assumptions (alpha):
  - Interface endpoints for core control-plane dependencies
  - Gateway endpoint(s) for S3
  - Opinionated security group pattern for endpoint ENIs
  - DNS behavior defaults and explicit escape hatches

Non-goals (for this ticket)
- Multi-cloud endpoint equivalents.
- Customer-specific DNS resolver forwarding rules (we only provide extension points / outputs).
- Full PrivateLink to customer services (only placeholders / outputs if needed).

Proposed default endpoints (alpha)
Required (default enabled)
- ECR: `com.amazonaws.${region}.ecr.api` + `com.amazonaws.${region}.ecr.dkr` (installer image pulls)
- S3 Gateway endpoint: `com.amazonaws.${region}.s3` (ECR layer storage + general artifact pulls)
- STS: `com.amazonaws.${region}.sts` (role assumption / IRSA flows, depending on customer posture)
- CloudWatch Logs: `com.amazonaws.${region}.logs` (cluster / installer log shipping when configured)
- EC2: `com.amazonaws.${region}.ec2` (EKS node / cloud provider interactions)

Recommended (default enabled, but allow disable via inputs)
- KMS: `com.amazonaws.${region}.kms` (if customer uses CMKs for EBS / secrets workflows)
- EKS: `com.amazonaws.${region}.eks` (for certain management flows; note some customers disable and use alternate management paths)
- Autoscaling: `com.amazonaws.${region}.autoscaling`
- Elastic Load Balancing: `com.amazonaws.${region}.elasticloadbalancing`
- SSM + related (optional, depends on whether customer uses SSM): `ssm`, `ssmmessages`, `ec2messages`

DNS behavior defaults
- Default `private_dns_enabled = true` for interface endpoints except where known to cause conflicts.
  - Rationale: pilots frequently fail when endpoint exists but private DNS is disabled; apps then attempt public AWS endpoints which are blocked.
- Provide per-service overrides:
  - `private_dns_enabled_overrides = { "ecr.api" = true, "ecr.dkr" = true, ... }`
  - `disable_private_dns_for = ["eks"]` (supported as a convenience input)
- Provide clear docs + warnings:
  - Private DNS requires the VPC to use AmazonProvidedDNS (or compatible resolver path). If customers have custom Route 53 Resolver rules or on-prem DNS forwarding, they must ensure *.amazonaws.com is resolvable appropriately.
  - Split-horizon DNS: enabling private DNS will override public resolution for that service inside the VPC; this is intended in private subnet deployments.

Security group pattern
- Create a dedicated SG for VPC endpoints ENIs.
  - Inbound: allow TCP/443 from `private_subnet_cidrs` and `cluster_security_group_id` (when provided).
  - Outbound: default allow all (AWS-managed) OR restrict to VPC CIDR only (TBD pending Security review).
- Inputs:
  - `allowed_cidrs` (list)
  - `allowed_security_group_ids` (list)
  - `endpoint_sg_id` (optional; if provided, module will not create one)

Module interface (inputs/outputs)
Inputs
- `vpc_id`
- `private_subnet_ids`
- `route_table_ids_private` (for S3 gateway endpoint association)
- `enable_endpoints` map (service -> bool) with opinionated defaults
- `private_dns_enabled_overrides` map
- `tags`
- `create_endpoint_security_group` bool (default true)
- `endpoint_security_group_id` string (optional)

Outputs
- `interface_endpoint_ids` (map as strings in README; implement as TF output map)
- `gateway_endpoint_id_s3`
- `endpoint_security_group_id`
- `enabled_endpoints` (for installer preflight / docs)

Acceptance criteria
- `terraform fmt` / `terraform validate` pass.
- `tflint` and `checkov` pass with documented exceptions only.
- Endpoints created across private subnets; S3 gateway endpoint associated with private route tables.
- Private DNS defaults documented, plus explicit examples for:
  - Fully-private (no NAT) deployment
  - NAT-enabled deployment with endpoints (hybrid)
  - Custom DNS / resolver forwarding (extension points)
- Integration test harness validates:
  - Required endpoints exist and are `available`
  - Private DNS flag behavior matches inputs
  - Outputs are wired for downstream installer usage

Dependencies / cross-team alignment
- Security guidance: confirm minimum required endpoints vs ‘recommended’ set and finalize SG egress posture.
  - Owners: Marcus Lin / Hanae Suzuki
  - Reference: Security review thread + “private-vpc logging defaults and SIEM hooks” for destinations that may require additional endpoints.
- Installer expectations: preflight must warn on missing ECR endpoints and private DNS misconfig.
  - Owner: Nina Petrova (installer constraints)

Links
- Confluence / Architecture
  - ADR-027 Terraform module boundaries and interface (for module surface area)
  - AWS private VPC reference architecture (EKS)
- GitHub
  - redwood-terraform PR: add vpc endpoints module + private DNS options (target PR for this work)
  - redwood-private-installer PR: detect endpoints and warn on missing ECR

Progress updates
- 2025-06-12 (Victor): Drafted list of required/recommended endpoints based on last 5 pilots + installer failure logs. Biggest recurring issues: ECR endpoints missing; private DNS disabled for ECR endpoints.
- 2025-06-17 (Marcus Lin): Security review note — ok with default enable for ECR/S3/STS/logs; wants explicit documentation around private DNS behavior and an escape hatch for enterprises with strict split-horizon DNS. Asked us to avoid creating overly-broad endpoint SG rules by default.
- 2025-06-20 (Victor): Implemented module skeleton + endpoint SG creation; added per-service private DNS overrides; added docs note on Route 53 Resolver.
- 2025-06-24 (Nina): Confirmed installer needs ECR api+dkr + S3 gateway endpoint in fully-private mode. Requested outputs be easy to consume in preflight (human-readable enabled endpoint list).
- 2025-06-27 (Irene): Approved approach to run heavy endpoint integration tests nightly; per-PR will run validate/lint/checkov and a lightweight plan test.
- 2025-07-02 (Victor): Merged endpoint module PR after addressing Security comments (restricted inbound to private CIDRs + optional SG IDs; clearer doc warnings).
- 2025-07-09 (Rafael Mendes): Verified in dogfood sandbox that installer preflight warnings match module defaults; confirmed no public egress required for baseline install when endpoints are enabled.

Follow-ups (not blocking Done)
- Add explicit matrix in docs: endpoints required per feature (e.g., CloudWatch logs enabled, SSM enabled, KMS CMK usage).
- Consider adding Route 53 Resolver query logging as a separate optional module (ties into audit logging story).
- Evaluate whether to default-enable `eks` interface endpoint; keep as recommended until we validate across more enterprise DNS setups.
